sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Level 1 it's actually possible to get priority as long as you space out Aatrox's abilities correctly. 
This should be relatively easy because he doesn't have his dash yet.

Do note that it is still possible to lose the all-in level one. Commit to a short trade, space out his Q's,
but don't commit long enough for his cooldowns to come back up.

- Level 2 is your strongest point in this matchup since your shield bash should enable you to win an 
all-in.

If you can find the opportunity to, fight him now.

- Level 3 and onwards, is all about spacing and baiting out his E dash, and then consequently punishing 
him with your own E into all-inning him until he is too far away to trade with effectively.

- Level 6 is when this matchup gets a lot easier because now, you can force to him to stay a certain 
amount of distance within you for as long as you get your E off.

- With Aatrox, your main goal is to try and punish his E cooldown by spacing back and forth out of his 
individual Q ranges.

- If he does E, all-in him until he's too far away to trade with effectively.

sections.heading: What to watch out for
sections.body:
- Look at his itemization because if he itemizes into Hex Drinker / Maw Of Malmortius, you should go 
Cosmic Drive rush to space out his Q's better and simultaneously time out his Hex Drinker / Maw Of
Malmortius shield.

This is pretty easy to do as your rush is Bramble Vest into Boots anyways, so you purposely delay your
build path for the sake of acquiring knowledge.

If he doesn't go Maw Of Malmortius, and instead goes basically any other setup, then your main goal 
is to now focus soley on bursting him down as opposed to playing towards a longer fight.

sections.body:
- Ulting Aatrox's W while it's attached to you will cancel it out since the projectile no longer has 
anything to latch onto.

Like- I know that it's considered to be a "useless ability," but it feels nice to cancel something that
impairs you anyways, no?

- In the mid-game, swap out bramble vest for oblivion orb if they have multiple sources of 
healing.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Give up early priority, you're outranged and walking up for CS while her Q is up is just asking for 
poke.

- At level 2 and onwards, try to bait out her charm by spacing back and forth behind minions and: if 
you can, try fishing for any potential E opportunities once said charm is down.

Otherwise: Just wait for level 6 to all-in her.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Ahri roots herself for a second when she uses her charm, so: if you've baited it out properly, you can
potentially look for an E -> Q angle.

But... most of the time it's just going to be a matter of running her down with Stormraider's Surge 
once you've gotten both your ultimate and some sort of way of closing the distance (Rocketbelt, Flash, 
etc.)

sections.heading: What to watch out for
sections.body:
- Try to avoid getting hit by Ahri's Q orb return unless you want a fistful of true damage splattered 
all over your face.
items: Try to avoid getting hit by Ahri's Q orb return unless you want a fistful of true damage splattered all over your face.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.body:
- As previously mentioned: her E cannot go through minions, so try and go in and out of cover from 
minions to try and bait it out for a potential all-in opportunity.

She should be relatively weak in the all-in.

- When Ahri ults, she has a slight lockdown period between her casts, if you're quick enough: you can
land a skillshot where she's going to be as she's dashing.

If you're not confident in landing said skillshot, just auto attack her because an auto attack will always
out-damage a missed skillshot, and you can always fire the skillshot at a more guaranteed opportunity
later if you need to.

- In the early game, only walk up to CS when her Q is down, otherwise: stand outside of her Q range 
and poke her down.

- Give up early priority, and play for a wave rebound with an HP advantage + minions, assuming you

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- If her shroud ever goes on cooldown, walk up and try commiting towards a longer trade, if she 
decides to fight you for some reason, then: exhaust her and run her down.

All of her damage comes from short burst trades rather than sustained battles, so you should be able
to win assuming you're at a high amount of HP to survive said initial burst.

- Your Q actually slightly outranges her Q, the problem is that it has a significantly longer channel
animation and you root yourself during said animation.

Now: usually, with a regular setup like Conqueror, this matchup would be extremely painful due to how
much more consistent her poke is, but with Deathfire Touch, you have more leeway to miss more Q's 
and still win assuming you space outside of her Q range semi-competently.

- When she goes for a Q -> passive procc, go for a W -> shield bash procc assuming your secondary 
meter is high.

(It's not exactly rocket science: In my opinion, this matchup is purely stat-based; whoever has the
better setup will win.)

sections.body:
- If Akali recasts her E from afar, Q towards her, however: If Akali recasts her E close to you, there is
a chance that she will try to go for an E -> R cast to move behind you instead of in front of you.

Now: this is a complete gamble and completely on  the Akali if she decides to commit to an E -> R, but
if you can predict it by Q'ing behind you, you'll be able to negate her outplay potential.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Level 1, you can theoretically gain priority, but this is one of the rare situations where I want you to 
actively give it up to set up your Level 2 all-in.

- Level 2, level up your W (as landing your E is basically impossible against this champion), and wait
for the Ambessa to waste her abilities for poke.

When she's wasted her Q1 and Q2, ghost and run at her immediately as she's effectively just exhausted
herself of any potential damage options.

If you get a kill from here, great! If you don't, pressure her until she has to recall in a bad wave state 
from the health deficit you gave her.

- Level 1, play patiently and let her get priority. If she dashes towards you, dodge it, and retaliate with
a Q.

If she keeps extending, keep fighting her, but don't leave yourself susceptible to getting hit by her Q on
her way out.

- Level 2, keep playing safe and keep punishing her if she overextends, the most important part about
this lane is getting the rebound off safely.

extended fights with PTA ASSUMING you save your Q until AFTER she's exhausted her options for dashes.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
Your #1 priority in this lane is to find a long trade into the Camille by any means necessary, this can 
be done in a number of ways:

-  You E her as she is walking close to procc her Q2 and then use your ultimate to make the realm more 
favored towards you and therefore limiting her escape options.

- You buffer your E during her E dash and then use your ultimate to make the realm more favored 
towards you. You CAN technically E after the stun wears off from her E, but this is a lot more 
inconsistent than just buffering her E CC. 

- You freeze the lane and when the Camille walks up, you E and then ult her.

- If you ult Camille's ultimate, then you'll be able to dismantle it.

then press the buttons to kill her right after. ( This tip is ESPECIALLY important if you ever want to 
dive her )

- Try to save your W for when her Q2 is up, your W has an annoying mechanic where it decays over 
time, so you want to ideally press W when she can burst you down the quickest.

- If you can, try to save your ultimate after she's used her E since it will yoink some of the bonus 
attack speed that she gets by using her E.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Give up early priority and just play towards your turret for the majority of the game.

If the wave starts rebounding back to her, shove the wave, let the wave bounce back towards you, 
and use TP as a get-out-of-jail free card if you get chunked too hard to secure the shove.

From here, just keep bouncing back waves and only play aggressive to secure a shove and
subsequent crash onto her turret.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Before you get Force Of Nature, you HAVE to wait for her to miss her Q (Noxious Blast),
from here: you will have 3.5 seconds (less if she builds CDR), to E her as she misses her Q,
and then start an all-in against her.

From here, land your follow-up Q, auto attack her, and then hard focus on using your
passive movement speed to dodge her next Q.

If you can manage to do that, keep responding to her missed Q's with your own Q's to make
sure that you're not rooting yourself for her to get a guaranteed Q onto you.

- Once you do get Force Of Nature: you can literally just turn off your brain and lazily all-in her
whenever you get the opportunity to do so. 

It's extremely overpowered into her, but you need to survive up to that point before being able to do so.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- If the wave is on your side of the lane, you can try Q'ing him from max range for additional poke,
this is easier to guarantee if you can time it as he's last hitting your minions.

If he ever misses his Q, feel free to E him and trade with him until he reaches 3 passive stacks 
onto you, and then: back off until his passive stacks run out.

- However, if the wave is not on your side of the lane, you have to hold Q until you know
that you are guaranteed to land it. If you miss your Q while overextended, you are dead.

When the wave is pushing out, walk up with the wave while having confidence, not with anxiety.

- If Darius is in lethal range (~50% HP) and he has no passive stacks on you: E him closer towards 
you and hug him for as long as possible to deny him from landing his Q onto you with the outer rim.

Alternatively, you can also flash or ignite him while he's about to land his Q onto you to deny his healing.

- If she misses her Q dart onto you, and instead: hit a minion, try to extend a trade for as long as

comes to get the most amount of uptime on your damage,

back up, in which you're (ideally) going to try to mitigate it's CC anyways via an ability buffer.

against her in a dedicated all-in.

- Walk up to the Garen and pressure him off the wave with your Q's,

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Level 1, go into the farthest bush to try and go for a level 1 cheese, 

Best case scenario: You chunk him for a lot of lane pressure.
Worse case scenario: He levels up his E and hops away which is still pretty good for you.

Then: play for the wave to bounce back, hold it, and then bully him if he ever walks up with your Q's
and E's, while backing off while they are down. If he recalls, push the wave and recall yourself. 

From there, just play safe until level 6.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Wait for the Graves player to use his E dash, and once he does use his E dash, this is your go-sign 
to start firing your own abilities.

- Stand behind minions for as long as physically possible against a Graves player since his auto attacks
are counted as projectiles, and minions can block them,

- Also: Stand away from walls so that Graves can't instantly procc his Q2 by having it's travel time
finished early against said wall.

- When Graves fires his Q directly towards you, walk towards the side, and then fire your Q so that
you don't self-root yourself for his Q2 to land on top of you.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Level one, take note of which ability she's leveled up as this will determine how you will try and use 
your range advantage to secure priority for level two.

- If she's leveled up her Q, try to tether right outside of her Q range and poke her while you're outside 
of it. 

If she Q's, and you spaced correctly, you can auto attack the minions while her Q is on cooldown.

- Once you hit level two, level up your W, and walk up as aggressively as possible to abuse your shield
bash damage.

- If she fights you now, you can win the all-in due to your ability to stat check her during this time.

- From here, keep playing aggressive until the level 6 mark, in which you should try to space out her 
abilities.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Prioritize movement over damage; use your abilities AFTER she's exhausted hers.

- You can throw out E's as she's going for CS, and if she dashes, walk exceptionally aggressively to try
and zone her with your shield bash damage and your Q damage.

- If she W's, walk into her W and fight her there.

- If she ults, auto attack her, wiggle side to side in front of her face to bait out another cast of her 
ultimate, and rinse and repeat until her ult is completely used up.

- And if you don't manage to dodge any of her abilities post level 6, there's a high chance that you

So: space correctly, and accordingly.

control of the wave (and subsequently a free amount of ramping Q stacks (1/3) on the wave) without
suffering a lot of poke damage from your Q.

- You can't really interact with an artillery mage in the early game in general, so: sit back, give up
lane priority, wait for the wave to get to your side of the lane, and play for the rebound back to his 
turret,

From there: either choose to recall for health or to stay in lane to not miss EXP.

to get back into lane so that you can play towards your level 6 powerspike.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- You can't exactly 'trade' with a Hwei due to his range advantage, I mean: I guess you could 
theoretically try to get an E angle after he uses his E fear, but most of the time: they aren't going
to just waste the ability for 0 reason.

- Just play safe until you get your level 6, wait for the wave to be on your side of the wave, swap one of 
your summoners for cleanse, and then just run at the Hwei until he uses his fear on you,

When he does that: use your cleanse, ult him, and then just kill him in an all-in. 
It's really just that simple.

- This matchup gets even easier once you get your rocketbelt and mercury treads powerspike since
you can just eat the fear, utilize the tenacity from your itemization and runes, and then just rockebelt
-> ult him -> kill him again.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.body:
- To avoid getting your ultimate canceled by Illaoi's ultimate, wait for her to either use her long Q 
animation OR wait to use your ultimate while she's using her E when you're mid-long range in relation 
to her. 

( Note: NOT short range E's because she can still get 
her ultimate off and cancel your ultimate ). 

This is because if you wait for these opportunities to ult, she will be locked out of using her ultimate until 
she's finished her respective animation making it so that she ends up being a free kill.

You can achieve this by going in and then backing out, most Illaoi players will follow your engage with 
a W -> E angle, and if you were able to create some distance, then now: you can ult during her E 
animation and then get her in the death realm without her E.

However, if the Illaoi is bad, she might not even know that this feature exists and just press R as 
soon as she presses E. 

If she ever does this: then you know that she's trolling and is now a free kill if you use your ultimate 
which turns this matchup from a 3 to a 2.

- If you can, try to start your ultimate away from bushes or lead him away from bushes in all-ins, 
so that he doesn't have access to any empowered auto attacks from his W passive.
items: If you can, try to start your ultimate away from bushes or lead him away from bushes in all-ins, so that he doesn't have access to any empowered auto attacks from his W passive.

gameplayRaw:
Early Game:

- Very similarly to a lot of ranged matchups, you want to just let the wave push into you since you're
realistically not going to be able to catch up to him to actually harass him, at least: not without it being
incredibly risky without your levels 1-3.

- Just preserve your HP, play for the rebound, recall, and then setup a freeze on your side of the lane 
so that he has to overextend to trade with you.

How to trade:

- Try to walk up as far as possible while still having a minion in front of you to block his root,

- If he ever auto attacks you, that's your go-to sign to fire out an E or a Q since his range is relatively
low at 475.

- As long as you are able to get a long trade into him, whether that's by waiting for him to use his root
and then hard trading into him, or if that's by closing the initial distance and then buffering said root,

You should generally be able to win all-ins against him.

What to watch out for:

- Post level 6, Ivern's ultimate, Daisy, can still traverse realms, which means that in any extended trade,
you are given a timer before Daisy proceeds to knock you up and Ivern proceeds to root you afterwards.

Meaning, that when Daisy is about to use her three-part knock up onto you, you want to try and time
your abilities right before it properly goes off.

If you are really good at this, you can even get your ultimate off as the projectile is spawning in the
normal realm to give yourself an extra buffer period.

Tips:

- If you can, try to start your ultimate away from bushes or lead him away from bushes in all-ins, 
so that he doesn't have access to any empowered auto attacks from his W passive.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Most Jarvan players will just sit back and spam Q pokes onto you until you get low for a lethal, which
is annoying, but it does mean you're most likely going to have easy access to the wave due to their
weak all-in potential.

- Therefore, before level 6, you should generally try to keep the wave rebounding back and forth, and
ideally find recall timers when you inevitably shove the wave into him.

- However, post level 6 is when you should have the wave be on your side of the lane since you now
have a way to force him into an extended trade with you via your ultimate.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- If the Jarvan is semi-competent, you shouldn't really be able to trade into him because he's just going
to spam max range Q pokes onto you and stay outside of your Q range.

- I mean, if you can punish his E and cooldowns respectively since he can no longer use his flag to get
out if he ever uses said abilities to poke you, then go for trades for as long as they can last for, but
that's probably not going to happen.

- Post level 6 is the only time when you're actually going to be able to trade into him, so just wait til then,
and then wait for him to use either his E or his Q for poke, and then just simply kill him after ulting him.

sections.body:
- As long as you don't troll your first three levels, you should probably be fine. Just let him push in, 
play for the rebound, shove the wave in, let the wave bounce back and just play for short trades 
until level 6.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Don't walk up too far if your W is down because otherwise you won't be able to negate the damage 
he deals with his ability rotations. 

- Hold your Q and your E abilities almost exclusively for the Jax, not the wave. 

If he spots you using Q or your E on the wave, then he's going to go in and then just hard win 
with an ability rotation.

- Wait for him to walk up and Q him on the head over and over again and just outplay him with your 
range.

- If he ever jumps in, just E him behind you, walk forward, and then go for a long trade while saving 
your ultimate for when he uses his E button.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Like any regular marksman matchup: sit back, give up lane priority, wait for the wave to get on your
side of the lane, and then play for the rebound back to his turret.

From there: either choose to recall for health or to stay in lane to not miss EXP.

If you're ever too low from the poke she's dishing out onto you, feel free to recall and use your teleport
to get back into lane so that you can play towards your level 6 powerspike.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- You can't exactly 'trade' with a Jhin due to his range advantage, I mean: I guess you could 
theoretically try to get an E angle after he uses his W root, but most of the time: they aren't going
to just waste the ability for 0 reason.

- Just play safe until you get your level 6, wait for the wave to be on your side of the wave, and then
just run at the Jhin until she uses his root on you,

When he does that: use your E, ult him, and then just kill him in an all-in. 
It's really just that simple.

- This matchup gets even easier once you get your rocketbelt powerspike since you can just eat 
the root, utilize the tenacity from your minor runes, and then just rockebelt -> ult him-> kill him again.

sections.heading: What to watch out for
sections.body:
- Don't recall in an exceptionally obvious spot if you're low hp, since some Jhin players like to go
ult snipes while you're recalling.

- If you're under 40% HP, recall and walk back to lane since you're most likely going to get dived by
the enemy jungler while the wave is near your turret.

It's literally their only win condition against you in this lane, so just be wary of that.

- Be wary of any wombo combo gank setups since Jhin can snipe you with his W for an easy follow-up
CC tool.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Before level 6, this matchup is INCREDIBLY painful if the Jayce spaces well. The only thing you can do 
against a Jayce before level 6 is to get a long lane, have him use his melee Q against you, E while he's 
midair, and then play for a long trade. 

However that is all dependent on whether or not the Jayce is stupid enough to randomly use his melee Q.

So just try to survive until you reach your level 6.

- Post level 6, this matchup is definitely more playable: 

Look to fish him with E -> R's and then run just: him down with your ultimate. 

Your goal in the mid-game is to get enough anti-kite via your rocketbelt to make it so that he cannot kite 
you and enough damage items be able to actually take him out with your DPS.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Unless the Karma suffers from an actual lobotomy in the middle of the game, there's not much you
can really do to threaten her due to her range advantage, her shield, and her W chain-root.

Just play safe, let the wave push towards you, play for the rebound, and keep bouncing waves back
and forth until you're able to get your ultimate + Mercury treads.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Stand behind minions and, emphasis on try: to land an E onto her if she wastes a Q on the minions.
You're probably going to miss, but: hey! It's worth a shot.

- Once you get mercury treads, rocketbelt, and level 6, (no, you are not going to be able to trade 
before then, welcome to Mordekaiser top lane), wait for the wave to be on your side of the lane, 
and then, walk excessively aggressively when Karma's Q is down.

If you can find the opportunity to: rocketbelt -> E -> R her and secure your E pull with your ultimate's
75% slow, from here: she's probably going to use her W onto you, in which case you should try to
time your Q as soon as you are rooted, to effectively negate it's CC.

Afterwards, once all of her abilities are down, utilize the movement speed gained from Stormraider's
Surge to run her down within your ultimate.

- Level 1, due to his range advantage with his Q's, it's difficult to secure priority, so just play save

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Before level 3, just play safe since you don't have enough damage to procc Stormraider's Surge which
is going to be when your all-in timers are going to be based around.

- Post level 3, if you can land an E, land it, Q them on the head, shield bash AA them, and then procc
Stormraider's Surge while using the movement to dodge as many Q's as possible from the Karthus.

Once your movement speed is about to wear out, gauge the situation:

- Is the Karthus low? (30% HP), then all-in him and kill him.
- Is the Karthus still high HP? (Above 30%), then just back off and play off your next Stormraider's
Surge procc.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Before level 6, he is incredibly punishable and incredibly immobile. 

Just wait for him to use his Q orb to farm for CS, and then just use your E to grab him and commit to
a trade for as long as possible.

If he ever walks up for CS, poke him. Is he going to use an auto attack? W and then shield bash AA 
him.

DO NOT let him breathe, because this is your strongest point against him.

- Post level 6, you generally want to have the same idea of punishing him whenever he farms, but you
need to now have the lane be on your side of the lane before commiting towards an all-in with your
ultimate.

- Additionally: try saving your skillshots until after you've seen Kassadin use his teleport so that you 
can ensure that your spells will land.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Level 1 is the only point of the game where you can consistently land skillshots against her, so try
zoning her out of the wave with your Q poke and secure level 2 priority.

- Level 2, rank up your W if she's close towards the wave since you're not going to be able to land
your E anyways, and threaten her with shield bash procc's.

If she's away from the wave when you hit level 2, you can theoretically level up your E for additional
poke, but this is pretty risky considering that you're lacking a massive damage and survivability tool
against an assassin in the early game.

- Level 3, crash the third wave, and go for a recall for a cheater reset or stay in lane to soak up EXP
until you've hit your level 6 powerspike.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Wait for Katarina to use her E dash, and then Q her before she's able to reset said E dash
by picking up one of her daggers.

If she's still in range for you to keep hitting her, use your W and apply a shield bash procc onto her.

That's it. That's all the counter play you can do against her. You can't do anything into her until she
uses her dash first, but if she doesn't use her dash, she's not really that threatening.

- Post level 6 is a diferent story though, since you can now limit her mobility down to only towards
you or and daggers that she's created.

Essentially: just wait for her to overextend into your side of the lane, and then try getting your
ultimate off before she's able to slip right past you.

- You're realistically not going to be able to land your Q's consistently into her, but that's okay.
Just auto attack her to death with PTA and dusk & dawn proccs in your ultimate, and you should be fine.

zoning her out of the wave with your Q poke and secure level 2 priority.

- Level 2, rank up your W if she's close towards the wave since you're not going to be able to land
your E anyways, and threaten her with shield bash procc's.

If she's away from the wave when you hit level 2, you can theoretically level up your E for additional
poke, but this is pretty risky considering that you're lacking a massive damage and survivability tool
against an assassin in the early game.

- Level 3, crash the third wave, and go for a recall for a cheater reset or stay in lane to soak up EXP
until you've hit your level 6 powerspike.

How to trade:

- Wait for Katarina to use her E dash, and then Q her before she's able to reset said E dash
by picking up one of her daggers.

If she's still in range for you to keep hitting her, use your W and apply a shield bash procc onto her.

That's it. That's all the counter play you can do against her. You can't do anything into her until she
uses her dash first, but if she doesn't use her dash, she's not really that threatening.

- Post level 6 is a diferent story though, since you can now limit her mobility down to only towards
you or and daggers that she's created.

Essentially: just wait for her to overextend into your side of the lane, and then try getting your
ultimate off before she's able to slip right past you.

- You're realistically not going to be able to land your Q's consistently into her, but that's okay.
Just auto attack her to death with PTA and dusk & dawn proccs in your ultimate, and you should be fine.

What to watch out for:

- Keep track of Katarina's itemization, if she's going on-hit: then you need to build mixed resistances,
but if she's building AP, then just build magic resistance items depending on how quickly she bursts
you down. 

(Priority list from high burst to low burst is: Kaenic Rookern, Spirit's Visage, and Force Of Nature)

Tips:

- Post level 6, try to save your E until after you've secured your ultimate and after she's used her
own ultimate to cancel her channel.

no longer have the ability to use her insane amount of mobility.

- You can't really interact with Lux in the early game in general, so: sit back, give up lane priority, 
wait for the wave to get to your side of the lane, and play for the rebound back to her turret,

From there: either choose to recall for health or to stay in lane to not miss EXP.

to get back into lane so that you can play towards your level 6 powerspike.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- You can't exactly 'trade' with a Lux due to her range advantage, I mean: I guess you could 
theoretically try to get an E angle after she uses her Q root, but most of the time: they aren't going
to just waste the ability for 0 reason.

- Just play safe until you get your level 6, wait for the wave to be on your side of the wave, and then
just run at the Lux until she uses her root on you,

When she does that: use your E, ult her, and then just kill her in an all-in. 
It's really just that simple.

- This matchup gets even easier once you get your rocketbelt and mercury treads powerspike since
you can just eat the root, utilize the tenacity from your itemization and runes, and then just rockebelt
-> ult her -> kill her again.

inside of your ultimate, in which case you can just follow through and kill him anyways.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- You can't exactly 'trade' with a Mel due to her range advantage, I mean: I guess you could 
theoretically try to get an E angle after she uses her E stun, but most of the time: they aren't going
to just waste the ability for 0 reason.

- Just play safe until you get your level 6, wait for the wave to be on your side of the wave, swap one of 
your summoners for cleanse, and then just run at the Mel until she uses her root on you,

When she does that: use your cleanse, ult her, and then just kill her in an all-in. 
It's really just that simple.

- This matchup gets even easier once you get your rocketbelt and mercury treads powerspike since
you can just eat the stun, utilize the tenacity from your itemization and runes, and then just rockebelt
-> ult him -> kill her again.

negated.

- This is unfortunately a matchup that you have to just lose until you've gotten your first item 
powerspike; Dusk & Dawn.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Naafiri is a really tough matchup since not only does her Q outrange everything your kit, but she
can also dodge any of your abilities with her W and her E.

invulnerability, from there: use your E and try to bait out her E dash,

When both her W invulnerability and E dash are down, only then can you use your Q against her.

-  If the Nasus goes up to Q, you Q him, if he goes up to auto attack, you W and then shield bash AA

- There's never really a time when you're going to be losing against a Nautilus top, you out-range him
and you out-damage him at every point of the game.

- Level 3 and wave 3, you should try to crash the wave so that you can get a recall off to play for the
rebound back to your turret.

- From there, just keep the wave on your side of the lane, and punish him whenever he walks up for 
CS.

- When you see Nautilus go for a hook onto you, buffer it with your Q, and try to pull him closer when 
he uses his root onto you.

kiting you out for another instance of his E shockwave.

- But: from there, he really shouldn't have anything else to defend himself with since his trades are 
very ability centric.

gameplayRaw:
Early Game:

- Whatever you do: don't die before level 6.

Let the wave push to you, play for the rebound back, crash said wave, and rinse and repeat until 
you've reached your level 6 powerspike.

Once you've reached your level 6 powerspike, you can actually threaten an all-in with ghost, but: it's
still pretty hard to kill her consistently until you've gotten your Rylai's + Approach velocity powerspike.

So just try to be patient, this is the hardest point of the game for you in this particular matchup.

How to trade:

- Stand behind minions and force the Nidalee to poke you down with her auto attacks which are 525 
range as opposed to your Q which is 625 range.

- When Nidalee auto attacks you, trade with a Q.

If you have your Rylai's + Approach Velocity powerspike, she should be slowed for long enough
for you to close the distance with the movement speed gained from approach velocity.

From here, try to use your E after she uses her Cougar W dash so that she can't avoid it, and then
just run her down.

If she's about to get back to her turret range, just ult her and force her to fight on even terrain.

wave, concede pressure and just wait for the wave to slowly push towards you.

- Give up priority early on, let the wave push into you, and just preserve your HP so that you can
effectively rebound the wave and get your first three levels.

sections.body:
- Similarly to someone like Fiora, you should generally try to only go for extremely short trades with your
Q and your W shield bash procc's until he's in lethal range.

If he doesn't his spell shield, he's dead anyways.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Ideally only play towards poking him out with Q's, until he's around 25% hp or less.

- If he's 25% hp or less; in lethal range, you can use your ignite and try to one-shot the Olaf with an 
all-in combo of Ignite + Q + Shield bash + AA to death with conqueror.

- If you're both level 6 and he overextends to your side of the lane, ult him instantly for an all-in.

The worse case scenario is that he ults early to deny your ultimate which doesn't really result in 
anything much since you can just easily walk away and back off.

The best case scenario is that he doesn't ult early, and you can secure a cheesy little kill near your turret.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.body:
- If the Olaf's ultimate is down, try using your ult as he uses his Q onto you to deny his Q cooldown reset.

- In the mid game, if you're both even, do not challenge the Olaf in the side lane. Just keep catching
waves and play towards outvaluing him in teamfights.

- In teamfights, try to grab Olaf's attention and force him to use his ultimate early.

If you are surrounded by his team, try to use your ultimate during his auto attack wind-up animation 
and ult literally anybody else except for the Olaf who's currently unstoppable.

If you are surrounded by your team, either: flash away from the Olaf or use Zhonya's if you have it.

The goal here is to try and nullify his ultimate as soon as physically possible.

- Also: make sure to buy anti-heal in the mid-game and politely ask your teammates to buy anti
shielding if their champions can allow for it.

If not: you may have to buy it yourself ( In which case: you should report your team )

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- If he ever exhausts his W poorly, you can 100% win a short trade, and if you manage to cancel 
his E with your own E (which is really rare), then you should be able to run him down and kill him.

But, against a good Ornn, you're probably not going to end up getting this opportunity since they're
just going to exclusively play for short trades and you don't have enough sticking power without your
ultimate to really threaten them.

Luckily, this does mean you're going to be able to control the wave, so try and keep the wave by your 
side so that you can find further opportunities to punish his weak all-in power before level 6.

Just keep dodging his Q's by moving back and forth, space out his W's by moving front and back,
keep track of the enemy jungler, and you should be relatively healthy for the level 6 mind games.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Try to stand right outside of his W range while you're poking him with your Q's, and if he W's 
early, back off temporarily to dodge the brittle procc, and then walk up to him and commit to a longer 
trade.

- Try to hold your ultimate until he's either in the middle of his E charge animation or until he's used
up his W.

sections.heading: What to watch out for
sections.body:
- Ornn has the ability to cancel your ultimate with his W, so don't use your ultimate if he has his W up
unless you're trying to deny his ultimate recast.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.body:
- If you're at high HP, and Ornn decides to ult you, try to E and subsequently walk behind him so that 
you can negate an additional brittle procc. 

This will result in you getting subsequently W'd for a second brittle procc, but this now enables you to
R him relatively safely since he no longer has any significant damage tools.

- If you're at low HP, and he's ulting you and you have the ability to deny his ult recast with your
own ult, feel free to ult him there, because even if he cancels your ultimate with his own W, it's still
a relatively worthwhile trade, so long as you time it perfectly around his recast period.

If you play it perfectly, he'll only be able to get a singular brittle procc onto you, and you'll be able to
commit to a harder trade because he no longer has any significantly powerful damage options.

Though, this does make it so that you waste exhaust your ultimate which is why I consider this option 
to be a last resort.

- If he ever jumps on top of you with W, then you can just buffer your E into it, and pull him backwards

sections.heading: What to watch out for
sections.body:
- Pantheon has the ability to negate your burst damage by using his E (Aegis Assault),

If he's close enough, you can try to Q at his current position and then flash behind him so that the 
damage comes from your new location instead of your old one, therefore: making it deal damage
against him.

Also: DO NOT use your shield bash auto attack while he's in the middle of his E animation unless you're
already behind him.

- He can use his ultimate to get out if he channels it right before your ultimate ends.

So try and use your E during the start of the fight, and then save your E as your ultimate is ending to
ensure he doesn't cheese you by escaping with his ultimate.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- All of your abilities outrange Poppy's abilities by large margin, so just play towards poking her down.

- However: it's INCREDIBLY hard to land your E onto a good Poppy player since she can easily
avoid it with her E dash or her W movement speed.

This issue can be resolved once you get your ultimate, since Mordekaiser's ult slows down
enemies by 75% during its cast time.

Meaning: If you can effectively combo your E -> R while Poppy's in the middle of one of
her animations, then you've secured yourself an all-in.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- When Qiyana uses her empowered Q for whatever reason, you should try to walk up and try 
commiting towards a longer trade, if she decides to fight you for whatever reason, then just exhaust
her and run her down.

All of her damage comes from short burst trades rather than sustained battles, so you should be able 
to win assuming you're at a high amount of HP to survive said initial burst.

- The same principle also applies if she were to dash aggressively on top of you; Q into her dash, shield
her Q projectile throw, and then run her down with exhaust and just: win.

- Her Q, unfortunately, outranges your Q, with the trade-off being that it's a lot more predictable.
When she has it up, try to wiggle around to dodge it, and then abuse it's early cooldown by walking up
and using your own Q.

Now: usually, with a regular setup like Conqueror, this matchup would be extremely painful due to how
much more consistent her poke is, but with Deathfire Touch, you have more leeway to miss more Q's 
and still win assuming you space outside of her Q range semi-competently.

- Remember to walk up with the wave level 1 so you can deny his level 1 proxy,

can WITHOUT sacrificing your own waves.

pressure against you with his base-kit, and he can't exactly force shove the wave the same way Singed 
can with his poison trail; he has to use his W and get the minions to hit him.

proxy off.

them so that you can re-match the mismatched tempo and continously force fights against him.

- When Rek'sai is in her unburrowed form, you generally want to stand right outside of her melee

all-in. 

Though, it's much easier to get a solo kill if you wait for her to create a new tunnel first before ulting.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- In terms of wave states, fight for priority level 1 if the Renekton doesn't pressure you off the wave.

If you get priority, level up W level 2, and walk excessively forward to pressure him off the wave, 
he shouldn't have enough rage to contest you and you'll be able to get some really good short trades
into him.

If you don't get priority for the wave, still level up W level 2 and look to fight him, he's either going to
level up his W, in which case you can hold your W until he's used his, or he's going to dash away with
his E, in which case: you can snag one last shield bash procc before he fully retreats.

In either scenario, try to farm up to 800 gold so that your next recall gets you a bramble vest.

If you get too low, and need to recall early, that's fine too. Just don't die.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Generally, in this matchup, you should try to extend trades for as long as possible since he tends to 
be favored in shorter trades due to his burst oriented nature.

- In essence: if you are both high hp, you're at the advantage, and if you're both at low hp: 
Renekton's in the advantage.

- Before level 6, your main goal is to try and save your E until after he's used his E dash, otherwise: 
just spam Q on top of him if he's already in-range of you.

If you're running shield bash (which you should), you can try to snag a little shield bash procc if he's 
under the 50 rage threshold for an empowered ability while he's not level 6.

- Post level 6, you can try forcing a fight with your ultimate either after he's used his dash or if he's 
near your turret since both instances will help guarantee a longer fight.

From here: whatever you do, DO NOT use your W while he still has his empowered W up unless you 
think you can one-shot him with a shield bash boosted auto attack.

- Stack up your W shield on the wave, and as the wave pushes out, wait for him to use his jump.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Before level 6, you want to try and utilize your range advantage as much as possible and stand right
outside of her E dash + Q dash range.

If you use your E while she's either doing her Q3 animation or when her E is down, you should be able
to play the fight out for a little bit until her cooldowns come back up with your shield bash auto attacks
and Q poke.

- Post level 6 and post plated steelcaps, assuming you're not heavily behind, you should be able to win
an all-in if you can get her to use her Q3 dash without taking an absurd amount of damage.

Ideally the combo is: E -> R while she's still in the air / locked in her Q 3 animation, (the R should 
buffer), and then auto attack her until she's used her E.

From there, start firing out your own Q's, and prioritize walking forwards instead of backwards when
her Q's come back up, and E close to yourself to create extra distance between the two of you as she
dashes past you to set up a follow-up Q.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Level 1, stand behind minions and try to secure priority.

Rumble's nature as a poke champion makes his all-ins pretty weak without his overheat passive, but 
level 1, he doesn't have the ability to procc it, so abuse that to its fullest.

- Level 2, level up your E if he's overextending towards the center of the lane, but otherwise: just level 
up your W and play for shield bash procc's if he ever walks in melee range to get CS / sustaining 
through his poke.

- Level 3, crash the wave and look for a reset if you can.

Even though you can win against Rumble in an extended trade (if his passive is down), it's hard to 
really to consistently get into range to apply said long trade.

So just stay behind minions, force him off of melee range to the wave with the pressure from your E 
and Q, and just repeat this cycle until he either overextends or until you've gotten your level 6.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
Before level 6, play as aggressively as possible behind the wave and try to time your E with his 
E pre-fire since it roots him for a split second.

If you can successfully land the E, Q him, procc your passive, and use your W for an extra shield bash 
procc.

You generally want to extend the trade for as long as possible UNLESS he has his overheat passive up, 
in which case you should focus on backing off instead of overextending.

Post level 6, you want to try and ult him either when his overheat passive is about to expire or when 
he's on a low amount of heat. Even with his ultimate up, he's no match for your all-in power assuming 
you can land your E during his E pre-fire animation.

If you have rocketbelt though, you can just straight up rocketbelt -> E -> R him whenever he's vaguely
in range and secure a kill that way too.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- In terms of wave states, if you can bait out and dodge her W poke, then generally: you should try
and pressure her off of the wave.

If you get priority, level up your W level 2, and walk excessively forward to pressure her off of the 
wave, and from here: try to get your W stacked up, if she tries to poke you, use your W shield off 
the damage and walk forward to try and use your shield bash AA against her.

If you don't get priority of the wave, still level up your W level 2, and just wait for her to use her poke
to then shield it and then attempt to go for a shield bash auto attack until your W shield meter gets
low.

In either scenario: you want to try and eventually getting a large wave to crash onto her turret, recall
and play for a rebound back to your turret to play for a freeze.

If you get too low, and need to recall early, that's fine too. Just don't die.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Generally, in this matchup, you should try to extend trades for as long as possible since she tends to
be favored in shorter trades due to her burst oriented nature.

- In essence: if you are both high hp, you're at the advantage, and if you're both at low hp:
then Sejauni's in the advantage.

- Before level 6, your main goal is to try and save your E pull until after she's user her Q dash, otherwise:
just spam Q on top of her if she's already in-range of you.

- When she's in lethal range (~20% hp), send out your E, and try to body block her from dashing out
with her Q dash.

- Post level 6, you can try forcing a fight with your ultimate until after she's used her dash or if she's
near your turret since both instances will help guarantee a longer fight.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Ideally, you want to try and poking him down with your Q while staying out of range of his E.

For context: Sett's E has 490 range even if he uses the pythagreom theorem; angles it to get the 
maximum distance. 

While Mordekaiser's Q has 625 range and Mordekaiser's E has a target cast range of 700.

- If Sett ever gets into melee range with you, press E backwards and send him flying away from 
you.

- When Sett is around 25% HP with no W charged up, this is your lethal range to commit towards an
all-in with your E -> Q -> W -> Shield bash AA.

- Sett's E can only stun you when he has another target to grab on the other side, but fortunately
for you: your ultimate can negate that by making it so that the only target he can use his E on is you.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.body:
- If Sett walks up to turret to hit it, don't trade into him too hard without your ultimate because he 
might be planning on diving you with his ultimate and charged up W.

Just Q him, and shield bash AA him, and then step back to see what his next move is.

If he dives you, his W shouldn't be charged up enough to kill you.

If he doesn't dive you, wait for his W meter to go back down and poke him down again with your 
E + AA's.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Level 1, walk with your wave, since some (mentally ill) Shaco players might try to go for a proxy onto
you, if they do try to go for it, fight them off.

- When the waves meet, you ideally want to fight for priority so that you can crash the third wave for
a cheater recall, and subsequently: a rebound back to your turret -> a freeze on your side of the lane.

- So long as you can get the Shaco to overextend in your territory, you should be fine to just beat him
down whenever he walks up for CS.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Trade for as long as possible against the Shaco until you start to go beyond unmarked and potentially
trapped territory. 

The last thing you want to happen against a Shaco player is to get feared by one trap -> feared by 
another trap -> feared by a recently placed trap, since it will chunk your HP down significantly.

- Just try to chip him down with max ranged Q's, and if he ever uses his Q invisibility dash, then look
to land your E (ideally while he's trying to use his own E poke onto you)

- You should be able to outsustain him as long as you use your W whenever he throws his E knife at you.

- Post level 6, when you see Shaco use his ultimate, identify which one is the real Shaco by seeing which
one takes more damage from your passive, and then proceed to ult the real Shaco to avoid getting
blasted by Shaco's death-clone-damage.

Bonus points if you can also time your ultimate while you're in an area with a bunch of pre-established
traps, since they will not follow him through the death realm.

sections.body:
- Be aware of the location of his traps at all times to avoid taking an unnecessary amount of damage.

- If you ever see the Shaco randomly use his ultimate, be ESPECIALLY aware of it's timer and existence,
since if you don't see it explode, there's a good chance he's going to command his clone to run away,
walk towards you, use his Q invisbility, make the clone look like it's him, and then have it explode on
top of you for a lot of damage.

Don't get cheesed.

- Don't get rage-baited, I know it's a Shaco, and I KNOW you DESPERATELY want to kill him, but if
you're low HP: recall, and don't greed for the kill because you're going to end up looking stupid.

- If you're forced to push the wave into him, be sure to walk behind your minions and linearly with 
your minions so that they can tank any incoming traps.

- Try to time your E pull during his Q animation to shorten it's duration or straight up cancel it if the
Sion doesn't release his Q early.

From there, just Q him on the head and then run him down until he gets too far away.

- Additionally: If you can buffer your Q or your R just when he's about to hit you with his ultimate,

that your ultimate has a cast-time, and by ulting him right as he's about to land on top of you, you'll

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- When it comes to trading with Sylas, the most you can do is just zone him out of minions whenever 
his Q (Chain Lash) is down with your own Q.

You can't really force a fight onto him with your E since he can just dash out of it with his E1 
(Abscond),

But it's not like he can dash onto you since you can easily just sidestep back into your minions and 
consequently punish him with your own E and extend said trade towards an all-in since his kit is 
oriented towards cycling his abilities for burst damage.

Just wait until you get your Dusk & Dawn and then win any fight he takes onto you.

Even if he dodges all of your Q's with his dashes and potentially his rocketbelt, it shouldn't matter 
anyways since you have Dusk & Dawn + PTA and can just auto attack him to death.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.body:
- In the mid game, most Sylas players just like to yoink Mordekaiser ultimate and ult anyone except 
for Mordekaiser in teamfights ( If they ult you, just ult him back and it's a free kill ). 

From here you have three options:

1. Ult someone else so that now, it's a 2v2 in the death realm.
2. Ult the Sylas before he can ult one of your hyper carries so that he's neutralized, you might 
actually lose the fight now, but at least your hypercarry can still contribute to the fight
3. You kill the Sylas after he leaves your ultimate and give him the PTSD that only Mordekaiser 
mains know of; being abandoned by your team after you kill someone in your death realm.

But yeah, he's not a hard counter to Mordekaiser because he will almost 100% lose an all-in against 
you ( unless you ult him first and then he ults you ).

Additional note: You can tell if he can use your ultimate or not based on the duration of the 
Sylas-ult-effect that's on top of you and if he doesn't actively have your ult showcasing next to his 
health bar.

If this is the case, then you can just ult him straight up with no worries.

120 splinter powerspike for as long as possible.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Stand behind the minions and try to play as aggressively proactively as you can while still being able
to dip behind the wave for cover from his Q.

Before level 6: If he ever overextends to Q you, land your E while he's self-rooted and commit towards 
an all-in.

Post level 6: If he's near your turret, you can ult him and save your E for when he goes for his W.

Alternatively, you can also try using your E to set up your ultimate to make it so that he never gets the 
opportunity to W (Abyssal Dive) towards an empty vision pocket to begin with.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Taric genuinely has terrifying all-in potential until you've gotten some sort of anti-healing to cut down 
his sustain.

- Give up level 1 priority, and play exclusively towards short trading with him.

- Level 2, level up your W and only fight him with your Q's and shield bash auto attacks.

- Level 3 is when the wave is going to start slowly rebounding towards him, assuming you let the wave
push towards you, make sure your HP is high so that you can effectively secure the crash.

Keep playing safe until you've gotten Oblivion Orb, and once you've gotten that powerspike, you can
expand your trade durations a little bit to make him use more of his mana.

If he gets low enough for an all-in to kill him (around 30% HP) or if he runs out mana, prolong the trade.

- Follow the same philosophy once you get your ultimate.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Before level 6, most of the time, you're not going to be able to find an all-in angle since Teemo's 
just so damn fast with his W movement speed, 

But: there is a slight window that you can abuse when Teemo goes for his auto attacks and Q 
animation respectively since both of them momentarily root him for a split second, which MIGHT 
be long enough for you to land your E and subsequently your Q for an all-in with your passive.

Try to trade for as long as possible until your W shield is about to break down.

- Post level 6: this matchup gets a lot easier since you can guarantee your E grab with your 
ultimate's 75% slow by combo-ing your E into your R when he goes for his aforementioned 
auto attack and Q animations.

Although: I'd recommend trying to save your ult for as long as possible until you're just about to 
run into a shroom, in which case: you can just ult it away.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Ideally wait for the Thresh to use his empowered E auto attack on the minions before walking up to
CS since you'll take more damage from his short trades if you don't.

- If he goes for an auto attack -> E pull onto you, respond with an ability buffer with your E -> Q and 
then just force an all-in until your W shield gets low since he's relatively weak in the all-ins.

Do note that some Thresh players might lean into lethal tempo for extra power in extended trades, 
in which case you should only commit towards all-ins while the wave is near your turret so that you 
have that extra buffer period to back off when your W shield starts to decay significantly.

- Post level 6: you should just be able to out-stat check him in any trades you go into him.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Ideally try to stand outside of his auto attack range and force him to use his E spin against you 
if he ever wants to trade with you.

- If he doesn't spin onto you, keep playing the neutral game and keep repeatedly poking him 
with your Q's over and over again.

- If Tryndamere does spin on you, use your W, procc your grasp + shield bash ontohim with an 
auto attack, and then E him away to then Q him on the head.

You never want to play fair; only play towards short trades until he's really low HP (30% hp), 
AND you have exhaust.

If he's in lethal range, try to time your E when he's in the middle of his auto attack animation 
(or if he's already used it), exhaust him when he's in range and pray that you have enough 
damage to get him to use his ultimate early.

If you can get him to use his ultimate early, run and stall for at long as possible: 
but not too far in case you can potentially snag a kill against him.

If you're successful in surviving, you can walk back and finish him off with a Q onto the head.

sections.heading: What to watch out for
sections.body:

amount of leniency you have when it comes to the duration of trades.

Grasp Tryndamere is only useful for the initial auto attack and should be traded with a little 
bit longer with your shield bash and passive before backing off.

Hail Of Blades Tryndamere requires you to keep the trade as short as physically possible to 
avoid tanking a potential triple crit combo IF he has a high amount of fury.

If he doesn't have a high amount of fury, you can afford to extend a trade a little bit longer, 
so long as he's engaging on your side of the wave.

not engage him until his ultimate is just about to run out

sections.body:

and destroy your entire base for free.

for a couple of seconds and then instantly kill him when he leaves the death realm.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Give up level 1 priority since Twisted Fate's range advantage and poke is hard to deal with before you
get your level 6 powerspike.

- Honestly: just sit back, let the wave push into you, and stay healthy enough to efficiently play off
the rebound back to his turret.

Once you get your level 6, you should be able to steamroll him by perma ulting him after buffering 
your E into his W stun card. 

So just play patient until then.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Try to time your E pulls for when Twisted Fate goes for auto attacks or tries to use his empowered W
auto attack, if you land it: Q him on the head.

- Post level 6: If he uses his yellow card on you, you should have enough tenacity to power through it, 
get your pull to land after buffering it into his card, and then you should just ult him and commit
towards an all-in.

Even if he goes AD Twisted Fate, he doesn't have nearly enough damage to genuinely contest you.

sections.heading: What to watch out for
sections.body:
- Look at his build to see if you need to go either plated steelcaps or mercury treads,

If he's going AD Twisted Fate: build plated steelcaps to nullify his all-in power.
If he's going AP Twisted Fate: build mercury treads so that you can both reduce his CC duration and
conveniently reduce his magic damage.

- Be sure to ping 24/7 when Twisted Fate is level 6 since he can easily roam onto your allies and 
murder them in cold blood.

sections.body:
- Just wait for the Twitch to momentarily root himself when he goes for an auto attack on you or the
wave and land your skillshots from there.

Try to trade for as long as possible until your W shield is about to break down.

- Post level 6: This matchup gets even easier since not only can you more easily secure your E grab with

attack animations, but he will also most likely use some sort of stat steroid before your ult lands.

- Level 1, sit back and let the wave slowly push into you.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- If it's an AD Udyr, DO NOT let him get into melee range of you since he will completely shred your HP
down with two quick awakened Q auto attacks.

unless you're 100% sure that you can kill him with an all-in lethal combo (15% HP)

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- In first wave, just sit under turret until the first three melee minions get low, and then once that
happens, walk up into EXP range, and if the Varus doesn't zone you out for this, you can even Q the
wave to get the gold from said minions.

- Afterwards, just try to preserve your HP and farm until turret, until the wave state begins to bounce 
back towards the Varus, in which case: try to use your minion wave advantage to secure a crash.

- From there, just keep playing safe and wait until your ult is up.

- Realistically, you're not going to get any good grab angles, unless the Varus is extremely stupid and

- If you have your ultimate, and he still has a tendency to keep walking up way too close, feel 
free to close the distance in whatever way you can (without using flash) and then all-in him.

- From there, just be wary of what you have to watch out for.

sections.body:
- Try to time your E pull for when Veigar for an auto attack harass or a Q harass onto you, and then
subsequently chase him down once you've landed your Q to procc your Stormraider's Surge.

bit more damage before backing off.

- If he decides to confidently walk up to you with his cage down, just engage on top of him and kill him
like normal.

cage and not even worry about it.

lane priority, wait for the wave to get to your side of the lane, and play for the rebound back to his 
turret,

From there: either choose to recall for health or to stay in lane to not miss EXP.

to get back into lane so that you can play towards your level 6 powerspike.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- You can't exactly 'trade' with a Vel'koz due to his range advantage, I mean: I guess you could 
theoretically try to get an E angle after he uses his E (Tectonic Disruption), but most of the time: they 
aren't going to just waste their only peel tool for literally 0 reason.

- Just play safe until you get your level 6, wait for the wave to be on your side of the wave, swap one of 
your summoners for cleanse, and then just run at the Vel'koz until he uses his E (Techtonic Disruption) 
on you,

When he does that: use your cleanse, ult him, and then just kill him in an all-in.
It's really just that simple.

(And yes: Vel'koz E can be cleansed since it's an initial knockup followed by a stun; a suspension.
It's basically like Nami W).

Ideally try to save your E pull for when he uses his ult, but you can't always guarantee that you'll
get the timing off.

- This matchup gets even easier once you get your rocketbelt since you can just rockebelt after him

- Vi top lane's entire gimick is to repeatedly charge at you with Q, procc hail of blades, and then back
off to poke you down with E's and utilize her high health regeneration to sustain through the lane.

damage while the wave is on your side of the lane.

Either way: you should be able be able to land an E pull and then extend said trade to your heart's 
content since a majority of her trade patterns from rapid instances of burst damage.

the next section of this entry.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- A majority of the time when you're trading against Viego, you want to try and focus more-so on 
avoiding his trade patterns instead of creating your own.

If he lands his Q onto you, stand outside of his follow-up empowered auto attack range, and wait for
the mark on top of you to wear off.

Once it wears off, walk up to get your own Q and shield bash trades while standing behind minions to
avoid getting hit by his W stun and follow-up empowered auto attack.

- Before level 6, you can more accurately land your E pulls if you can time it when Viego is in the middle
of his empowered auto animations or while he's in the middle of channeling his W, which slows him 
down by 10%.

- Post level 6, this matchup gets a lot easier since your ultimate just ends up out-statchecking him a
majority of the time.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.body:
- To prevent Volibear from canceling your ultimate with his own ultimate, you should try timing your
ultimate through his Q windup animation since while he's Q'ing, he's locked out of using his other abilities
for a small time frame.

Now: if you mess this up by either ulting him while his hands are in the air (too late) or if you mess this
up by ulting him just a bit too soon, then you're probably going to die without your ultimate. 

So: don't mess up.

Do note that most Volibear players will combine their E and Q together, so if you ult away his E, then 
he's going to be left without his shield.

If he's a tank volibear player, this won't matter nearly as much since he has a ton of defensive stats.

But if he's an AP Volibear player, this is essentially a death sentence.

sections.heading: What to watch out for
sections.body:
- Warwick can stop your ultimate in two ways, the most obvious application of this 
is him ulting your ultimate and becoming unstoppable.

But most of the time: the Warwick ends up moving way too fast which makes it unreliable for
him to ult at you to cancel his ultimate, so if they ever try canceling your ult with their ult, it's
most likely to just run away. Which: is annoying, but: hey! At least his ult is down now.

( And! You can aura farm him in all chat with a singular question mark to assert dominance
because he's evidently very much scared of you if he's only using his ultimate to run away from you. )

The less obvious way he can do this is by using his Q while your ult is being cast.

The reason why this works is because of some mysterious spaghetti code where instead of giving
him a regular dash, it decides that the best course of action is to make him both simultaneous exist 
and not exist at the exact same time!

Making it so that even those it looks like he exists, he's actually just temporarily invulnerable to all 
forms of CC, which includes your ultimate! YAY! ISN'T THAT FUN??? ( No, not it isn't )

So, if you want to avoid suffering from Schrodinger's Cat syndrome: 
then try and ult him while he doesn't have any targets to latch onto or until after he uses his Q.

- Whenever he walks up to the wave, Q him on the head and try to prolong the trade with auto attacks

- If Wukong ever dashes into you, keep auto attacking him until your passive comes up and keep in 
mind that he has the ability to W out.

damage.

- If Wukong ever W's away from you, E him back towards you and prolong the trade until he gets
too far away to keep chasing.

- Post level 6: you can force the fight to go for longer without worrying about him reaching his
turret by ulting him while he's using E dash animation.

sections.body:
- You can't really interact with an artillery mage in the early game in general, so: sit back, give up
lane priority, wait for the wave to get to your side of the lane, and play for the rebound back to his turret,

From there: either choose to recall for health or to stay in lane to not miss EXP.

If you're ever too low from the poke he's dishing out onto you, feel free to recall and use your teleport
to get back into lane so that you can play towards your level 6 powerspike.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- You can't exactly 'trade' with a Xerath due to his range advantage, I mean: I guess you could 
theoretically try to get an E angle after he uses his E stun, but most of the time: they aren't going
to just waste the ability for 0 reason.

- Just play safe until you get your level 6, wait for the wave to be on your side of the wave, swap one of 
your summoners for cleanse, and then just run at the Xerath until he uses his stun on you,

When he does that: use your cleanse, ult him, and then just kill him in an all-in. 
It's really just that simple.

- This matchup gets even easier once you get your rocketbelt and mercury treads powerspike since
you can just eat the stun, utilize the tenacity from your itemization and runes, and then just rockebelt
-> ult him -> kill him again.

sections.heading: Early Game
sections.body:
- Level 1, you can easily secure priority due to your significantly stronger level 1.

- Level 2, level up your E if he gets too close to the wave for an all-in with level priority,
but otherwise: just level up your W and walk aggressively to zone him out with your W shield,
and subsequent shield bash procc threat.

- Level 3, is when you're going to have to start keeping track of the amount of currently 
active ghouls that he can summon up.

If he has enough for 3-4 ghouls, back off, and focus on being erratic with your movement to
avoid getting poked down by his E, and especially to not get caged in by his W.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Before level three: try to walk up and zone him off as many minions as possible,
If he walks up, all-in him until either you get a solokill or he backs off the wave.

- From level three to level five is when you need to time your aggressiveness with how many
graves he has set up / how many minions he can potentially create by hitting you with his E.

If it's 2 or less, you shouldn't be too scared and can keep on playing on the aggressive by
zoning him off of the wave and force him to decide if he wants to try and poke you down
with his E (which shouldn't do much since he doesn't have too many graves up),

or if he wants to farm minions with his E, in which case you can play even more aggressively
and try to zone him off of EXP range entirely.

- Post Level 6 is when you should try to close the distance as much as possible without using your
ultimate, whether by with good movement, cheating it with rocketbelt, or by using your E.

( Typically after you bait out his E, or when he uses Q on the wave and temporarily self-roots himself ).

Your main goal here is to try and be as proactive as you can to force him to use his cage early
against you.

If he does use his cage, this is your go-sign to ult him immediately and commit towards an
all-in.

Just don't get poked down too hard before that opportunity arises.

- If you can't close the distance for an all-in post level 6, no worries: just sit back and keep
poking down his maiden with Q's or E's until you've gotten your Rocketbelt so that you can actually 
be able to consistently close the distance.

sections.body:
- There's currently a bug in the game where if you kill the Yorick while you're in the death realm, and 
his Maiden is up, then the Maiden will just not die???

However, even though it's still alive, when Yorick respawns,

or every single instance of a Yorick maiden is dead.

So make sure to kill the Maiden after you kill the Yorick, because otherwise: 
you're going to get bombarded by his harem.

Just be sure to save your next E for if the Zac wants to escape with his own E ( Elastic Slingshot ) 
after you both leave your ultimate.

sections.heading: How to trade
sections.body:
- Zed isn't exactly a champion that you trade with just purely based on the nature of his W 
(Living Shadow), so just play safe until you've reached your level 6 and dusk & dawn powerspikes.

Once you've gotten to those respective points, ghost at him when he's on your side of the lane and
auto attack him with shield bash + dusk & dawn procc's until he's used his ult on you.

When he does that, you can go for a Q directly on top of his head, unless he can recast his W, in which
case you should just for an E and keep hitting him with dusk & dawn procc's until he's exhausted all
of his mobility options so that your Q has a higher chance of landing.

- You can't exactly 'trade' with a Ziggs due to his range advantage, I mean: I guess you could 
theoretically try to get an E angle after he uses his W (Satchel Charge), but most of the time: they 
aren't going to just waste their only peel tool for literally 0 reason.

once he uses his W satchel -> ult him -> kill him again.

you can buffer your E or your Q into her stun to effectively negate it's duration since both your
Q and your E self-root you anyways.

- Try to wait for Zyra to setup her plants before commiting towards an all-in with your ultimate 
against her since they'll dissapear in your death realm and will consequently reduce her damage 
significantly.
